Dark Verse #1

Predator

RuNyx, Maria Adam (Translator)

3.97
157,527 ratings20,924 reviews
Rate this book
Ce se întâmplă când o forță de neoprit întâlnește o putere imposibil de clintit, într-o lume unde moartea dictează regulile?

În adâncurile întunecate ale mafiei, Tristan Caine este o enigmă. Singurul membru al Organizației Tenebrelor care nu face parte din familie, el rămâne o prezență misterioasă pentru toți, cu abilități de neegalat, o moralitate discutabilă și motivații greu de înțeles. Este letal și știe acest lucru.

La fel și Morana Vitalio, fiica liderului unei familii rivale, ale cărei competențe în tehnologie sunt la fel de periculoase ca măiestria lui Caine în lupta cu armele. Morana se infiltrează în casa lui Caine cu intenția de a-l elimina, fără a ști că între ei există o legătură strânsă, un secret de douăzeci de ani gata să iasă la iveală. Ura, pasiunea și istoria trecutul se ciocnesc, stârnind scântei neașteptate.

Dar o amenințare mult mai mare și mai înfricoșătoare apare la orizont. În ciuda resentimentelor care îi separă, doar ei pot înfrunta acest rău devastator.
    GenresDark RomanceRomanceEnemies To LoversDarkMafia RomanceContemporarySpicy

About the author

RuNyx

19 books23.5k followers
RuNyx is a New York Times, USA Today and international bestselling author of romance. Her stories range across subgenres from dark contemporary to gothic to historical to fantasy and more, and are currently being translated into over 10 languages.

Her pen name has a very special meaning to her. When she's not writing, she's reading, traveling, meditating, daydreaming, and most of all, procrastinating.

Reread #2

"You ever put a leash on me, I’ll fucking strangle you with it."

I have to say this book was the perfect start. It's categorized as a dark romance and when I think of dark romances usually all the come into my mind are fucked extra smutty books but this really changed my perception of them. This one was heavy on the plot and it made it so well balanced with smut. This planned and executed really well, it was clear that the author knew what she was doing because this series is a hit. It's also so gripping because its not easy for me to reread book and I sometimes get drawn away but the hold that this had on me was mind-blowing because I had to force myself to stop and you know its a good book when you to force yourself to stop. Runyx made this series so special.

"Tristan Caine terrified her, but it wasn't because of the death he was bringing her slowly, the death he would bring her one day, the death he raised in her. No. It was the life."

It's the way this series is written. Runyx has this amazing writing style that brings out so many emotions of characters in different ways that hit so hard in all the right places and I feel like that should really be appreciated and truth be told this series is very underrated when you compare it to other dark romances when it's clearly very superior to them. It's not even that!! its the way she marketed these book sm the way she gives us more insight on her stories and tells us canon things that draw us even more to the characters like during this reread I felt so much closer to the bond that Tristan and Morana had with their vehicles and also Its just the way the chapters are long but they dont feel long at all. It's also third person and I love that but the way she wrote it feels like first person because its overall just so well done. I do think many people dont like this book as much as the others but this just has a special place in my heart because I never ever feel this way with the characters and the world that she has created.

"He'd had her pinned against the wall with her own knives at her throat."

Let's talk a little about the tropes 🙈
It had so many blushworthy forced proximity scenes.
So much mutual pining.
Knife to the throat scenes.
It's a perfectly executed enemies to lovers.
Very hot constant staring.
Who did this to you?.
She falls for him first but he falls for her harder
Protective MMC.
Badass FMC
Found Family


"Tristan Caine was toast. But he was one smooth toast."

Tristan is one of the MMC that had me in a chokehold form the start to the finish. He was such a complex, mysterious character that I honestly was very intrigued by, his mysterious nature and his clouded past had me wanting to know more about him, turned into learning more about him which led to me falling deeply in love with his character. Him riding a bike did not make hisi case because that shit was 🥵. Also his outfits were so good??? Like man's fashion is truly classy. Also when he calls Morana wildcat 🙈🥵 the nickname slapped. I fely so sad for him and I wanted ot give him the biggest hug becuase he was just a kid, he deserves so much better. I loved how he cared for Morana with his subtle touches and the way it was showed in this book was beautiful also the part where he would ask if he had hurt her had me scremaing. Also him climbing a wall to meet her?? Amazing!! I like his character even more in the second book and I felt a void without his pov through out the series so im very excited for the syndicator.

"One day, I'm going to carve your heart out and keep it as a souvenir. I promise."

Morana is hands down the sexiest dark romance female lead right after Amara and Lana Myers. She was so hot and her being a hacker did help her case, Why she really intrigued me was because I'm also in that field in a way. Her character arc and her journey was very well expressed and her relationship with Tristan was so awesome. Her snarky attitude and her smartness is what differentiates her from everyone else and it was just something to root for. I like how she did not back down and stood up for herself, I think dark romances have really lowered the standards for female characters so I liked seeing them being raised. Morana's point of views are so well written, its basically told from her point of views throughout and the things she does and say and thinks made it all so much more interesting. I was fully invested istg.

"When it comes to death, you are mine"

This was definitely dark and the romance was very angsty and spicy so I think that was done very well. To make the book perfectly smutty and keep the romance enjoyable with teasing. Heartwrenching scenes and interactions between them that will read so good. The scene in the bathroom?? I was sweating just reading that. The banter that they both said, the way they both communicated with their eyes. How they refused to believe the tension between them but it just built it up more? There are so many scenes that these two share that I am in love with.

"A small part of Morana could not help but admire that lethal, powerful grace."

Side characters: As of now there were only two prominent ones Dante and amara and I love them so much amd ok their book is the best so I'm looking forward to rereading it and honestly I loved their interactions and Dante was just so perfect his wit really brought out the life in this book. Amara and her friendship with Morana was also one of the things that I liked

Scenes that I loved:
`Morana and tristans bike scene
`The bathroon scene
`tristan climbing up the wall
` the scene where its raining and morana is looking out the window
` the flashbacks

Overall, its a very well written dark romance novel!

– 2.4 stars

What this book has:

💫 a heroine in a mafia setting with a brain
💫 a heroine who is not just waiting for her father to arrrange a marriage for her
💫 a dark hair, blue eyed hero with BDE
💫 a hero who doesn't speak much
💫 enemies-to-lovers

What this book also has:

📌 3rd POV
📌 endless monologues
📌 staring so MUCH STARING 👁👄👁
📌 SILENCE
📌 guns and violence
📌 did I already mentioned staring? if not, yeah, a lot of staring 👁👄👁
📌 blue eyes
📌 a motorcycle
📌 the words "TRISTAN CAINE" (219 times to be exact)
📌 a voice of whiskey and sin (that was not used nearly enough)
📌 I wanna do this review for The Predator justice so I gotta mention once again the eye staring contest Tristan and Morana had going on throughout this whole book 👁👄👁
📌 no talk, only stares 👁👄👁

Not to compliment myself, but I think I did a good job of summarizing The Predator. If something is missing from that list, my DM's are wide open for suggestions. 😇
A staredown. She didn't remove her eyes from his, and he didn't remove his from hers, neither willing to look away first.

Basically this whole book in a nutshell:

Morana Vitalio: Stop staring.
Tristan Caine: No.

I wanted to say that reading this book was such a great experience, but just looking at the rating, that would be a big lie. It was painful af. The first 40% of this book were hands down a solid 1.5 stars rating from me. The monlogues, the eye starring, the silence I hated everything about it. It was so mind-numbing. The voices in my fucking head talked more than the characters in this whole book. 😭💀

Tristan had the potential to be up there with all the great heroes. Is there anything this man can't do? But due to the writing I couldn't care enough about him. Same applies for Morana. For the first 40% I was just begging for someone to end my misery (I'm dramatic ik just let me 🤡🤚) that by the time when something interesting between the main character happened I was like



Tristan fucking Morana in the restroom while her father's men are standing behind the door calling out to her? Yeah, even I can admit that scene was something. If I had to choose my favorite scenes from this book, then it probably that one or the Tristan & Morana rain kiss in the last chapter. That were the scenes were I was mourning this couple potential, cause they could have slapped so hard and end all other mafia couples, but nah sorry missed that mark with all the staring instead of talking.
"Next time, I'm going to see how loud you can scream, Ms. Vitalio. I'm going to make you so sore you won't know if it's from the screaming or the fucking."

Ugh. See? R.I.P. the potential of that man. I'm mourning. Honestly, I wish I could love him more, but the way this book was written destroyed everything and was so boring. 😭



There was actually an interesting flashback scene between Tristan and Morana that I somewhat enjoyed, until I got to the point where it was revealed why Tristan hates Morana that much. And oh boy.. oh hell. Here is my reaction:


He stilled even more, impossibly.
She stilled even more, reflexively.
The air between them stilled, dangerously.

I really wanted to put a sweet TristanMorana quote here, but all my highlights are 90% from them staring at each other across the room while crickets are chirping in the background or 10% fucking. That's it. 😬

Conclusion

The first half was pretty much a disaster, the second half was somehow better, but I still don't care enough. Usually I'm all about the side characters, but even Dante and Amara didn't do anything for me, because I'm already dreading how the writing is going to be 💀 I'm still going to read the next books, but for now I need a break. 🏃🏻‍♀️

❥ 𝓂𝒾𝓃𝒾 𝓅𝓁𝑜𝓉 𝓈𝓊𝓂𝓂𝒶𝓇𝓎:
morana vitalio is a very smart and dangerous woman determined to find out the truth about a 20 year old mystery that resurfaced. this mystery leads her straight to tristan caine, one of the most feared men in the enemy’s mafia. she’s intent on killing him, but after trying and failing she quickly comes to realize that he’s an important piece of the puzzle. what happens when two worlds filled with so much hate, collide?

❥ 𝓂𝓎 𝓉𝒽𝑜𝓊𝑔𝒽𝓉𝓈:
i absolutely loved this book. one of the best enemies to lovers i’ve ever read. when book 1 is them as enemies and just based off the end you know book 2 will be them as lovers. literal chef’s kiss. the slow burn…the fucking TENSION. i still feel hot from reading it. there’s nothing better than sexual tension between two people who actually hate each other. ate it up. the plot was so so so entertaining…the mystery mixed in with it all? yes. it keeps you hooked and on the edge of your seat. AND IT MADE ME CRY!? the entire package, this book isn’t missing a thing😭i read this because it was a short dark romance to get out of my slump. i did not expect to fall in love with this universe and i can’t wait to continue because that ENDING!? let me just say🫦

❥ 𝓌𝓇𝒾𝓉𝒾𝓃𝑔/𝓅𝒶𝒸𝒾𝓃𝑔:
was the writing perfect? absolutely not. idk if it’s just my copy of the book, but there were so many typos. they were very easy to correct in my head, but that’s really my only complaint about the book. not a big enough of one to drop a star, but i just had to mention that😩it’s written in third person…we all know how i feel about third person and guys, i’m gonna have to stop hating on it after this series because wow. it truly depends on who writes it tho and runyx did it so well. was i craving dual pov so bad? yes, but it honestly made me feel more of the enemies aspect since you’re only reading one pov. it was sooo fast paced! i swear once i hit the 50 page mark, i blinked and was at the end. i can’t even remember how long the chapters were, but once you start this book…i promise you won’t want to stop.

°❀⋆.ೃ࿔*:･

Well, i have had this series for some time now but it never really piqued my interest but after one of my good friend spoke so highly of it i finally decided to give it go and let me tell u it didn't disappoint. Although the writing was typically lousy and boring but i can ignore it because the characters were soo good and the storyline was excellently executed. The plot was pretty interesting as well and kept me wanting to read it more and more.

So in this captivating narrative, we're immersed in the world of two influential families, the Vitalios and the Maronis. Morana Vitalio, Gabriel Vitalio's daughter, is a computer expert who has created some codes, which found in the wrong hands could cause a war between the two families. Enter Tristan Caine, also known as 'The Predator,' a protege of Lorenzo Maroni. As Morana and Tristan uncover the truth behind the theft, they realize they're pawns in a larger game. Together, they form an unlikely alliance to retrieve the stolen codes and prevent potential harm to both of the families.

Although the pacing of book was very good and kept me intrested because something was happening all the time but the writing was lousy, bland and repetitive, there were countless mentions of his whiskey and sin voice and also his blue eyes and with every single mention i wanted to throw my book because it became way too much like once or twice would've been tolerable but it was literally more than twenty times and this might be the only reason im not rating it five stars because good writing literally matters to me the most. This book is considered dark romance although i couldn't feel the romance at all but man the sexual tension between them was off the charts ngl i could literally feel it through the pages.

╰┈➤ Tristan Caine

This guy embodied all the classic traits of a dark romance lead: mysterious, brooding, and haunted by a troubled past. As I delved into his backstory, I couldn't help but feel a wave of sympathy wash over me. His struggles and hardships gave context to his guarded demeanor and quiet disposition. It became clear why he was so hesitant to trust or open up to others. In the end, I found myself rooting for him to find the closure and peace he so rightfully deserves.

"They called him the predator. His reputation preceded him. He rarely went on hunt but when he did, it was over.”

╰┈➤ Morana Vitalio

Morana stands out as one of the most memorable female leads I've come across. She embodies beauty, intelligence, and a fierce determination that commands respect. What truly captured my attention were her sharp wit and fearless demeanor—her snarky comments added a delightful flair to her character. However, there were moments when her reactions felt a bit exaggerated, especially when she couldn't resist his intense gaze. Despite this, her intelligence and unwavering resolve remained admirable throughout the story.

Morana's upbringing in a mafia family shaped her into a strong and independent woman from the start. Despite being surrounded by dangerous men, she fiercely fought for her freedom—a refreshing departure from the typical portrayal of women in mafia romances as submissive and doormat types.

"She'd been raised around sharks. And she’d learned not to bleed"

Despite being constantly surrounded by people, Morana experienced deep loneliness, with no one truly there for her when she needed support the most. It was heartbreaking to see her endure so much hardship when she deserved nothing but love and understanding.

"She cried because she had no one to give her a shoulder and hold her as she cried, because she had to wrap her arms around herself”

What actually disgusted me the most was morana's shitty father istg that man was such a fucked up piece of shit. He basically always prostituted and humiliated his own daughter in front of other men like I can't imagine a dad not snapping the neck of the man who tried to touch his daughter in a wrong way but this man he literally sat there when some other man tried to touch his own daughter and then proceeded to be an ass about it and let's not even forget about him fucking throwing her down the stairs just because he was angry istg she could've died but he gave no fucks about her, istg such a terrible piece of shit.

It's undeniable that this book was a captivating read from start to finish, keeping me hooked with every turn of the page. And let's talk about that iconic rain scene! Despite not fully understanding the hype beforehand, experiencing it firsthand had me completely swept away. It was steamy and intense in all the right ways, leaving me absolutely hooked.

"He devoured her in the rain, with his gun beneath her jaw."


°˖➴ "Overall, if you're craving a gripping read that will captivate you from start to finish, look no further. Dive into this book and let yourself get lost in its compelling storyline. Enjoyy!!" 💌

While an entertaining and binge worthy read, it had some flaws which I can't overlook, as they made a direct impact on my enjoyment levels.

✅What I liked-

1. Romance- The chemistry between Tristan and Morana is so good. I liked how it wasn't insta lovey and it gradually intensified and developed. The two had such good moments together, I was giggling and blushing. The spice was hot.

2. Characters- Tristan and his mysterious persona kept me engaged. I wanted to find out the reason for his hate and I was not disappointed. I loved how he carried himself, the man exudes power and he knows it. Morana was interesting, I liked her complexities with her father. But at the same time, she was dumb af for someone who's supposed to be smart.

3. First half- The thing about codes was an interesting storyline and to see it get abandoned so quickly in the second half was a buzzkill.

4. Amara and Dante- Look, I liked Tristan and Morana but I know for a fact I'll love Amara and Dante more. In the few scenes they have together, there's already far more chemistry between them and I know it's gonna be angsty. I need more of them.

❌What I didn't like-

“Don’t you know not to run away from predators, sweetheart? We like the hunt.”


The Predator is an enemies-to-lovers masterpiece—a dark and intense story about two lonely and flawed people, a tale of violence and retribution, of love, hope, and healing. The plot is gripping and intense, with brutal and horrific details that expose the dark side of humanity and society.

“I don’t know whether to snap your neck or fuck the life out of you.”


This series stands apart from other dark romance books, offering a more thrilling, gory, and violent experience, where unexplained mysteries about their world enrich the plot and captivate attention from the very start. RuNyx’s writing is poetical and engrossing. She masterfully orchestrated the events in this book, meticulously constructed the plot, intricately wove Tristan and Morana’s tangled and tumultuous histories, and beautifully explored their present relationship and their hatred for each other. It was absolute perfection.

Morana ‘The Wildcat’ Vitalio, a mafia princess and a nerdy tech girl, is smart, fierce, and independent. All her life, Morana dreamed of two things: freedom and love—yet she got neither from the man who called himself her father. She is lonely and alone, even when surrounded by people in her house. But slowly, she begins integrating herself into Tristan’s dangerous world, finding safety and solace in her enemy’s home and his friends. I love the way she carries her strength and hope in her heart. I’m happy she finally has people in her life who care about her and love her.

“The man who’d claimed her death had given her a glimpse of life by doing something he probably didn’t even realize he’d done.
In that moment, the enemy had done what no one had ever even tried to do for her.
He had made her feel a little less lonely.”


Tristan ‘The Predator’ Caine is ruthless, intimidating—a hunter in a man’s clothing. A silent man who can kill with nothing but his powerful aura and piercing glare. Tristan has a traumatic past, one that cannot be healed because his dangerous nature was exploited by others for their own gain. He became a monster because that was what people expected of him after the event that destroyed his life. I fell for him instantaneously. The way he helps Morana, keeps her safe, even though his only motive in life is to kill her—speaks volumes about his love and obsession for her. Also, the man cooks, clean and ride a motorcycle? I am in love.

“No one else gets to kill you, Ms. Vitalio,” he spoke quietly. “The last face you see before you die will be mine. When it comes to death, you’re mine.”


Tristan and Morana started as enemies in this book, with their knives at each other’s throats—it was a very romantic first meeting, honestly. They are bound together by their tragic pasts, each consumed by their desire for revenge and vengeance. Despite their motives and efforts, they find themselves irrefutably drawn to one another, giving in to their desires and relentless obsessions. Their intense eye contact and stolen glances played a major role in establishing their hidden and suppressed feelings for each other.

“We’ve been honest so far, Ms. Vitalio,” he murmured. “I’ll be honest now. I despise you but I want you. Fuck it, I do. And I want you out of my system.”


They have a convoluted relationship—Tristan wants to kill Morana, yet he saves her every time she needs to be saved, and she runs to him for comfort and safety whenever she’s in danger or hurt. There are so many layers to their relationship, making it even stronger and more intimate, and I love how RuNyx is slowly peeling back each layer, exploring their bond in such intricate detail. Tristan and Morana are one of the best couples I have ever read about—no one can beat these two.

“I don’t want to fix him. I want to fix me. And he’s the only thing that seems to be working.”


That kiss in the rain is one of the best scene in this book. It’s a literary masterpiece for me, the most beautiful kiss scene I have ever read in my life. Hands down. It was painful, beautiful, aching, and comforting. That scene had me screaming and crying.

“He kissed her – without his tongue, without his hands, without his body. Just his lips – soft, firm, present – on hers.
It was the most beautiful kiss she could have ever dreamed of, the most untainted she’d ever imagined from him, with a softness she’d not thought him capable of. With his intensity, with his blazing eyes, the silent promises had been of devouring.
This wasn’t devouring.
This was savoring.
He was savoring her lips, memorizing her taste, introducing himself to her so much more intimately than he ever had.”


The plot twist was unexpected and heartbreaking. My heart shattered into pieces after learning the truth behind Tristan’s hatred, and for Morana, not knowing anything. They have a long way to go to build a strong foundation for their love and happiness. I can’t wait to see where this series takes me next and what other truths RuNyx is going to unearth, but I am here for all of it—and more.

➙ Second read: October 2024 — 5 stars
➙ First read: January 2023 — 5 stars

We follow two families, the Vitalio's and the Maroni's, our female main character, Morana Vitalio, Gabriel Vitalio's daughter, is a computer expert and has created some codes, which found in the wrong hands could cause a war between the two families. Those codes are stolen, when Morana tracks them, they lead him to Tristan Caine, also known as “The Predator”, Lorenzo Maroni's protege. But they both quickly realize that someone is trying to frame Tristan unfairly and they will be forced to team up.

┏━✦❘༻𝓹𝓪𝓬𝓮 𝓪𝓷𝓭 𝔀𝓻𝓲𝓽𝓲𝓷𝓰༺❘✦━━┓

The pacing of the book is very good, it's fast, things are happening almost all the time and it keeps you 100% interested in what will happen next. Now, the writing, although it is simple and easy, it did seem somewhat repetitive and erratic, but I can understand it since, being from Morana's point of view, her mind works like that. Now I will talk a little about romance and smut, if you are not comfortable with this, you can skip to the characters area, lets be responsible readers.

The romance did not convince me much, it seemed to me that there was more sexual tension than anything else, it is true that, after understanding certain things towards the end of the book, Tristan's behavior can be understood a little more, but the Morana's is a bit... weird lmao. He basically dedicated himself to observing her, the whole book was a staring competition, I'm worried about his vision, should I give Tristan some glasses?
About the smut, i found it.. weirdly hot? LMAO. Like I didn't even know how to feel about it half of the time, since he said things like “I don't know whether to snap your neck or fuck the life out of you” AND I WAS LIKE SIR???

┏━✦❘༻𝓬𝓱𝓪𝓻𝓪𝓬𝓽𝓮𝓻𝓼༺❘✦━━┓

🕸✘𝓜𝓸𝓻𝓪𝓷𝓪 𝓥𝓲𝓽𝓪𝓵𝓲𝓸✘🕸 She is a total badass, a strong and independent woman from beginning to end, who has had to grow up surrounded by horrors and has still managed to be so amazing. She is snarky as fuck and doesn't take anyone's shit, but she is very lonely. DID I MENTION SHE IS SO FUCKING INTELLIGENT?? Cleans intense drooling. I really loved her.

“She'd been raised around sharks. And she’d learned not to bleed”

“She cried because she had no one to give her a shoulder and hold her as she cried, because she had to wrap her arms around herself”

“I don't think anyone can handle you. “Not if you don’t want to be handled”

🕸✘𝓣𝓻𝓲𝓼𝓽𝓪𝓷 𝓒𝓪𝓲𝓷𝓮✘🕸 He must have had 20 dialogues during the entire book, but… mmm well! He stares a lot!! Ok ok poor Tristan, let's stop bullying him. He is a very mysterious character, you never know what he is thinking or what his next move is going to be. he has the traumatized vibe and in some parts I really felt sorry and sad for him, he is also very lonely. He deserves a hug.

“They called him the predator. His reputation preceded him. He rarely went on hunt but when he did, it was over.”

“Damn it, the man was a book of blank pages written in invisible ink that she had no idea how to discover”

🕸✘𝓓𝓪𝓷𝓽𝓮 𝓜𝓪𝓻𝓸𝓷𝓲✘🕸 We didn't get much of him but I'm so excited for that!! I can't say a lot about him, but I really really liked him!!

🕸✘𝓐𝓶𝓪𝓻𝓪 𝓡𝓸𝓼𝓼𝓲✘🕸MY BABY. She was truly a friend to both Morana and Tristan and she deserves the world.

“In another life, in another world, she could actually have been friends with Amara. But she wasn't in another life or in another world. This was her reality. And her reality was alone.”

I will definitely continue with the series, especially because the plot is super interesting, I don't know if I will venture into more dark romance for now but if you have any good recs that will not traumatize me, let me know!! I hope to read The Reaper very soon!!

If tension could cut? It would bleed tristan and morana because I could never maintain the intense eye contact that was going on between them lol talk about next level sexual tension 🤭

I was entirely hooked on everything that added to the plot here when it came to the romance, crime, mystery and action. Even in the middle, where the changing dynamic of the characters was emphasized on. I should add how I’m not a fan of third POV or long chapters but i didn’t mind it here

if you like a brooding enigmatic mmc, whose actions speak louder than their words, with blue eyes and whose voice is said to be of whiskey and sin (as morana likes to say), then —Tristan is your man. his sense of resistance yet vulnerability given his tragic backstory was notable through said actions. He’s for sure down bad for Morana but he was limited in being able to express that

morana and her moments of defiance with Tristan and anyone (though reckless at times), assertiveness, and how genuine and valid her worries and doubts felt about everything, all contributed to my enjoyment of her character arc. could say I almost adored her and see the potential for that to grow. Some things were repeated a few times, however it didn’t bother me having already known. the author also stresses this early on and attributes it to her high IQ.

tristan & morana these two had almost little dialogue and far too many gazes, but I fully understood how that spoke for them. their moments of searing tension and angst were actively felt with this sense of animosity yet the lines were blurred, and I ATE ALL THAT UP 😮‍💨 I thought they matched each other’s energy in the masks they wore to ensure their survival well—until it started to slowly slip. booked felt like each others equals tbh. I can’t wait to see their relationship develop further as we got the enemies turning into lovers by the end 😩

dante & amara i need to know more about both of them. Amara seemed like the kindest soul and I liked the possibility of her and morana being friends 🥺 I also felt the allure with Dante with how protective him and Tristan are.

I wish I could say more but I'm trying to remain as vague aside can. However, tristan’s reason was a surprise, even though I was right about certain connections. and that moment at the end in the rain with that kiss was EVERYTHING. omg. needless to say, I see the potential of this being an addictive series for me. I could see why some love and aren’t fond of this as it isn’t without its faults, but I personally was soo invested in the characters and their stories. it was something different that I needed and I can’t wait for more.

★ 4 stars

Enemies to lovers and they are actually enemies? SOLD.

This was such a fun read, it's been awhile since I enjoyed a mafia series despite me loving them, it's really hard to find one that isn't overdone. Every time my feminism goes out the window for a morally grey man🧎‍♀️

Morana Vitalio is a strong heroine. I loved that the author gave her a fiery strong personality and didn't make her like every other docile mafia princess. She's a coder and she is constantly doing badass things she shouldn't be. She answers to no one.

“She'd been raised around sharks. And she'd learned not to bleed.”

Tristan Cane... where do I begin and how do I get him stalking me outside my window? taking applications. I'm not sure if he's really that hot or I just like him because he hardly speaks? 🤭 No but seriously, he's super sexy and the chemistry and tension between these two was consuming every page. The shower scene?! don't even get me started 😮‍💨 I loved learning about his backstory and I'm interested to see this elaborated in the following book. I'm hoping we see his POV more as it was lacking in this book.

“Don't you know not to run away from predators, sweetheart? We like the hunt.”

The ending took my by surprise and I loved the cliffhanger. I'm curious how there story will continue in the next book. I will definitely be continuing the series because it seems it will only improve.

Overall I was unsure about this at the start as it's a slow burn, for a relatively short book, however, I'm glad their story is written over two books so it didn't feel rushed. The writing is okay, a little repetitive at times but the tension and chemistry is what made this book an exciting read. This had an interesting plot that kept my attention and I didn't find it overly predictable. While there was some spicy/steamy scenes, it's didn't consume the whole book (probably 3 scenes max) and there was a lot more offered by this book than just smut which appealed to me.

I can't wait to continue and see more about Amara and Dante, because that woman is an angel and deserves the world and Dante is a snack 🍩💅

"Don't you know not to run away from predators, sweetheart? We like the hunt."

For all my GR besties who have driven me to finally read this I thank you so much because OMG was that a fun ride. What can I say about this book that has not been said before??? This is the true definition of enemies to lovers. The tension you feel between these two characters is EVERYTHING!!!! The man hardly even speaks and you still feel every ounce of the tension and that is what we love! That is what people who love the "enemies to lovers" trope crave when they read it. I mean come on....Our FMC Morana is trying to kill Tristan in the very first chapter! How can we not love this?? Runyx did an amazing job keeping me on the end of my seat wondering what was going to happen next between the two main characters.

Then these men in this book "swoon". I honestly can not decide who I love more but at the end of this one I am going to say Tristan. I loved Morana she is intelligent and has so much sass and fire in her. I even love Amara, she is the epitome of a "girl's girl". I love that the two girls found friends in each other. I was addicted to every word on the page and couldn't stop. I was completely hooked and invested into the story from the mafia, to the romance, to the violence. I could go on and on about this book and describe all the characters in more detail but I want you to experience what I did and to love the character's through reading about them. Plus I need to be done with this review so I can get back to reading the second book🤣🤣 All you need to know is I am OBSESSED!

If I was to give this book any critism it would be that the chapters felt forever long and the third POV is not my fave! However, this did not take away from how amazing and addicting this story is. I will leave you with some of my favorite quotes though.
